about: A workflow every account can find and run: when the person records a launch (what launches and on what date), plan it as a content campaign backwards from that date: build the list first, then tease, hype and collect, then a blitz in which every channel and every supporting voice posts inside one short window after the lead post, and read the numbers back afterwards. One workflow-recipe row in the shape of the shared recipe shelf (job, input_schema, ordered steps, each with do, submit and checks), with the wake that starts it.

payload.label: Plan a launch as a content campaign
payload.job: When the person records a launch, read that launch record, plan the campaign backwards from its date in four phases (build the list, tease, hype and collect, blitz), write a blitz runbook in which every channel and every supporting voice posts within the first 30 to 120 minutes after the lead post, draft every post natively for its platform from one message, check every word against the person's own rules, get the person's approval of each post exactly as it will go out, schedule only approved posts in the person's own scheduler or hand them to the person, and after the launch read the numbers back against the targets the plan set. The AI drafts and schedules approved posts only; the person approves every word and owns every account.
payload.produces: A dated launch calendar with its teaser, hype and blitz posts drafted per platform, and after launch a readback of what each phase brought in.

source.from: a principles registry mined from video captions
source.name: Run a launch as a content campaign planned against real milestones; fire the launch inside one short window; launch often; announce publicly what you will do
source.note: Adopted: the phase order (list, tease, hype, collect, blitz), the 30 to 120 minute window for every supporting post, launches as recurring content moments, and the public promise turned into follow-up pieces. Not adopted: posting from accounts the person does not own or asking supporters to hide that they are connected to the launch; every supporting voice posts as itself.

launch_record.description: The id of the person's launch record: it holds what launches, the launch date and time with its time zone, and the offer

channels.description: The platforms and owned channels the person posts on (for example an email list, a video platform, a social feed)

supporting_voices.description: Other accounts that agreed to post at launch (partners, co-founders, customers), each named as the person names them

list_target.description: How many sign-ups the person wants on the list before launch day

steps.title: Read the launch record and the person's past launches
steps.do: Read the person's launch record named by the input launch_record with the records read (records:read with { "id": <launch_record> }), and copy exactly: what launches, the launch date and time with its time zone, the offer and its price if the record holds one, and the person's reason for launching now. Then list the person's earlier launch records (records:list with { "type": "launch" }) and, for each one that has numbers, copy its list size before launch, its launch-day sales or sign-ups and its dates. Never fill a field the record does not hold: write "not in the record" and ask the person for it with tool:tell-the-person before going on.

steps.title: Plan the four phases backwards from the launch date
steps.do: Count back from the launch date in the read-launch step and put dated phases on the calendar, in this order: (1) list: an owned sign-up place (a waitlist page or the person's email list) with one reason to join now, open from the first date until launch; set the list target to the input list_target, or, without one, to the best earlier list size from the read-launch step and say so. (2) tease: pieces that show the problem and the making of the thing without naming the offer. (3) hype and collect: pieces that name the date, show the thing working and ask people onto the list; include one public announcement piece that promises what will happen at launch, with the check-in pieces that keep that promise. (4) blitz: launch day. Every phase has a start date, an end date, the channels from the input channels it uses, and a number to reach (sign-ups for list and collect, replies or saves for tease and hype). No phase may start after the launch date.

checks.says: Every phase uses only channels the person posts on

steps.title: Write the blitz runbook: every voice posts within 30 to 120 minutes
steps.do: Write the launch-day runbook as timed rows from the lead post. Row 1 is the lead post at the launch time from the read-launch step, on the channel with the most reach. Then every other channel from the input channels and every supporting voice from the input supporting_voices gets one row, each at an offset of 30 to 120 minutes after the lead post, spread so that no two rows share the same minute. Each row names the channel or voice, its offset in minutes, what it posts (the lead post shared, its own piece, or an email to the list) and who presses send. A supporting voice posts as itself, from its own account, and says how it is connected to the launch.

checks.says: Every channel has a row in the blitz
Every supporting voice has a row in the blitz

steps.title: Draft every post natively per platform from one message
steps.do: Write one message for the whole campaign in one sentence: the problem the launch solves and why now (from the read-launch step). Then draft every post the phases and the runbook need, each from that message and written natively for its platform: its own first line, length and tone for that platform, never the same text cross-posted. Each draft names its phase, its channel, its date and time, and its words. Teaser drafts do not name the offer. Every number in a draft comes from the read-launch step or is left out.

checks.says: Every draft belongs to a planned phase
Every phase has at least one draft
Drafts name the channel each goes out on

steps.title: Check every word against the person's own rules
steps.do: Call tool:check-against-a-persons-rules-and-verdicts once per draft from the drafts step, with the draft's words and the person's own rules and verdicts records as that tool's input names them. Copy each finding. Rewrite every draft that has a failing finding and check it again, until each draft passes or the person's rule says it needs the person's ruling.

steps.title: The person approves every post exactly as it will go out
steps.do: Show the person, in the chat, the phases, the blitz runbook and every checked draft exactly as it will be posted (channel, date and time in their time zone, words). Ask for each draft: "Do you approve this post exactly as written?" Wait for the answer. Change only what they ask, check the changed words again with tool:check-against-a-persons-rules-and-verdicts, and show them again. Record approved and not approved drafts by id; never treat silence as approval.

checks.says: Only drafts that were written can be approved

steps.title: Schedule only the approved posts, or hand them to the person
steps.do: For each approved draft, if the person has their own self-hosted Postiz (tool:github:gitroomhq-postiz-app) with that channel connected, schedule it there at its date and time and copy the scheduled post's id. Otherwise call tool:tell-the-person with the draft's words, channel and exact time so the person posts it. Give each supporting voice from the blitz runbook its own row's time and words with tool:tell-the-person, for the person to pass on. Never schedule a draft that is not approved, and never post from an account the person did not connect.

checks.says: Every approved post is scheduled or handed over

steps.title: After launch, read the numbers back against each phase's target
steps.do: After the blitz phase ends, read the list size, the launch-day sales or sign-ups and each post's views, replies and saves from the dashboards the person connected or from the person (ask with tool:tell-the-person; never guess a number). For each phase write its target from the phases step, what happened, and one sentence on why. Write the result into the launch record's history with the records write, and name the follow-up pieces the public promise from the hype phase now owes. Then call tool:tell-the-person with the readback.

checks.says: Every planned phase is read back
